scope_findings.claim: The project is structured as a single experienced researcher (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova) and a single academic beneficiary (ELTE Budapest) jointly applying under MSCA-PF.
The fellowship is classified as a European Fellowship (EF) with the researcher moving from Bulgaria (Plovdiv, BG) to Hungary (Budapest, HU) — an intra-EU mobility move.

Excellence and international mobility are the defining characteristics of this application: the fellow is an experienced researcher moving from Bulgaria to an EU Member State (Hungary), satisfying the core scope criterion of the instrument.
The requested fellowship duration is 24 months (European Fellowship).

The research domain is precision agriculture / data-driven crop management: uncertainty-aware multi-sensor diagnosis of crop water stress (root-zone soil moisture, crop water status) and probabilistic irrigation decision support for tomato crops using Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and PlanetScope Earth observation data fused with ERA5 meteorological reanalysis and field measurements.

The project implements a two-way transfer of knowledge: the fellow brings plant physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise (the project's biological ground truth) to the host's geoinformatics group; the host provides remote-sensing, hyperspectral imaging and multisensor-fusion methods and infrastructure to the fellow.

Training integrates MSCA-PF mandatory transferable dimensions: digital and AI skills (including the responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding), knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship (translating the uncertainty-aware decision-support demonstrator toward user uptake), and research integrity and open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation).

Training prepares the fellow for increased research collaboration and information-sharing via digital technologies, including open access publication, FAIR data management, and open research software practices, evidenced by the open validation protocol and the open-science posture of the demonstrator.

A Career Development Plan is prepared jointly by supervisor (Dr. András Jung) and fellow (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova), submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24.

The dissemination and career development plan includes ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host, ≥120 hours of transferable-skills training, and a follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship end.
AgroVIR (Hungary) is engaged as an associated partner providing farmer access, field validation and feedback at Hungarian tomato sites; it is not a co-beneficiary or co-applicant.
No secondments and no non-academic sector placements are included in the project design; the project runs for the full 24-month EF duration at the single host institution (ELTE).

The project does not involve Euratom research areas (the domain is agricultural remote sensing and irrigation decision support); Euratom-specific eligibility conditions (SR-11, CC-14) are therefore not triggered.

The budget regime is unit_cost; the EU contribution is derived internally from confirmed effort months (24) multiplied by published MSCA-PF unit rates and the host-country coefficient for Hungary (HU), with no per-project call-level ceiling stated in the call documents.
The TRL target is a research prototype (TRL 3–4), appropriate for a 24-month single-researcher fellowship; magnitude claims for societal and economic impact are stated proportionate to this TRL.
